bad.spl: index=security sourcetype=ids_alert earliest=0 | stats count by signature

samples.explanation: The classic zombie: scheduled every 5 minutes, earliest=0 rescans all of retention each run, and the search itself is disabled — still occupying a scheduled-search slot definitionally, invisible until someone audits.

good.spl: index=security sourcetype=ids_alert earliest=-24h | stats count by signature

samples.title: Sample - All Time Zombie Alert

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats count by host | appendcols [search index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats avg(bytes) by host]

samples.explanation: appendcols stitches columns by row position, not a key — different ordering or lengths misalign every value. Computing both aggregates in one pass by the key is correct and cheaper (no second dispatch, no positional risk).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats count avg(bytes) AS avg_bytes by host

samples.title: Sample - Appendcols Positional Join

bad.spl: * | stats count by host

samples.explanation: A bare * retrieves everything the platform allows — no lexicon terms to intersect, no bloom elimination. Anchor with index + sourcetype + a term.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=200 | stats count by host

samples.title: Sample - Bare Star Retrieval

samples.explanation: Scoped retrieval, then enrichment: the lookup applies only to events that survived the indexed filters.

good.spl: index=network sourcetype=fw_traffic action=blocked | lookup asset_inventory ip AS src_ip OUTPUT owner | stats count BY owner

samples.title: Sample - Bounded Lookup Enrichment

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined earliest=-90d | timechart span=1d count

samples.explanation: I/O scales linearly with the window. A 90-day window on a search consumed daily pays a ~13x multiplier over the 7 days that answer the question.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined earliest=-7d | timechart span=1d count

samples.title: Sample - Broad Time Range

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | collect index=summary

samples.explanation: collect has no dedup intelligence — re-running over an already-summarized range duplicates every row. Drive it from one non-overlapping schedule (low).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats count by uri_path

samples.title: Sample - Collect Duplication

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | dedup clientip | stats count

samples.explanation: Without sortby, WHICH event survives dedup is order-dependent and it runs on the SH. stats latest() by the key is deterministic and map-reducible (low).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats latest(_time) AS last by clientip

samples.title: Sample - Dedup Without Sortby

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=404 | delete

samples.explanation: delete is irreversible, frees no disk, and hides data from every search. It never belongs in a scheduled or ad-hoc analytics search — the safe intent is a scoped read. Never installed as a demo search.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=404 | stats count by uri_path

samples.title: Sample - Delete In Search

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 daysago=7 | stats count by clientip

samples.explanation: daysago= is a legacy modifier documented as valid but slated for removal; the snap-aware earliest/latest form is precise and future-proof (low).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 earliest=-7d@d latest=now | stats count by clientip

samples.title: Sample - Deprecated Time Modifier

bad.spl: index=web | head 1000 | search status=500 | stats count by uri_path

samples.explanation: head is centralized streaming — placing it before the status filter drags the unfiltered stream to the search head, then throws most of it away.

good.spl: index=web status=500 | head 1000 | stats count by uri_path

samples.title: Sample - Early Centralized Commands

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status!=200 | stats count by status

samples.explanation: Exclusion (field!=x) can't use the lexicon the way inclusion can — Splunk retrieves candidates then discards them, and != also drops null-field events.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined (status=404 OR status=500) | stats count by status

samples.title: Sample - Exclusion In Base Search

bad.spl: index=* *error* | transaction host | table host, _time, _raw

samples.explanation: The on-stage query: three anti-patterns stacked — scan every index, defeat the lexicon with a leading wildcard, then assemble transactions from the unfiltered stream on the search head. The rewrite scopes retrieval and replaces transaction with stats.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status>=500 | stats earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen count BY host

samples.title: Demo - Act 4 Live Critique

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | rex field=_raw "(.*)error(.*)fatal(.*)"

samples.explanation: Multiple .* in one rex forces backtracking across full _raw for every event. Anchor with negated classes ([^,]+) and extract once into named fields.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | rex field=_raw "error=(?<err>[^,]+)"

samples.title: Sample - Greedy Regex Over Raw

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by clientip, uri

samples.explanation: stats by a near-unique field (uri) builds one bucket per value — SH memory scales with cardinality. Aggregate by the dimension you actually report on.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by status

samples.title: Sample - High Cardinality By

bad.spl: sourcetype=my_source | lookup my_lookup_file D OUTPUTNEW L | eval E=L/T | search A=25 L>100 E>50

samples.explanation: The canonical pipeline-order example: A=25 belongs in the base search, L>100 immediately after the lookup that creates L; only E>50 must wait for the eval. Filtering last transforms rows that were always going to be dropped.

good.spl: sourcetype=my_source A=25 | lookup my_lookup_file D OUTPUTNEW L | search L>100 | eval E=L/T | search E>50

samples.title: Sample - Late Filtering

bad.spl: index=web *error* | stats count by status

samples.explanation: *error* bypasses the lexicon and bloom filters — every term in every bucket is examined. An anchored field filter restores index-time elimination.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=5* | stats count by status

samples.title: Sample - Leading Wildcard Search

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | lookup http_status_desc status OUTPUT description | stats count by status

samples.explanation: The lookup enriches every raw event, but its output (description) is not used by the stats — so it can move after the aggregation and match a handful of grouped rows instead of every event (low: cost).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by status | lookup http_status_desc status OUTPUT description

samples.title: Sample - Lookup Before Aggregation

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | head 50 | map search="search index=app host=$host$"

samples.explanation: map dispatches a separate search per input row — a concurrent search storm that skips OTHER scheduled searches. Restructure to one search with a key.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats count by host

samples.title: Sample - Map Command Explosion

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined host=web*prod-01 | stats count by status

samples.explanation: A wildcard spanning punctuation (host=web*prod-01) fights the segmenter and can silently match differently than intended. Match whole segments or TERM().

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined host="webserver-prod-01" | stats count by status

samples.title: Sample - Mid Token Wildcard

bad.spl: index=app log_level=ERROR | stats count by component

samples.explanation: An index filter alone pulls every event class in that index. Adding sourcetype narrows the lexicon walk and downstream extraction (low: advisory).

good.spl: index=app sourcetype=app_logs log_level=ERROR | stats count by component

samples.title: Sample - Missing Sourcetype Scope

bad.spl: index=network 10.1.2.3 | stats count by action

samples.explanation: A raw IP is segmented on the dots; TERM(10.1.2.3) matches it as one lexicon term instead of intersecting four segments.

good.spl: index=network TERM(10.1.2.3) | stats count by action

samples.title: Sample - Missing TERM for IP

bad.spl: index=app env=prod ERROR | stats count AS errors | append [search index=app env=prod WARN | stats count AS warns] | append [search index=app env=prod INFO | stats count AS infos]

samples.explanation: Each append re-dispatches a search over the same index — three reads where one suffices. conditional aggregation over a single OR'd base search reads the data once.

good.spl:
index=app env=prod (ERROR OR WARN OR INFO) | stats count(eval(searchmatch("ERROR"))) AS errors
  count(eval(searchmatch("WARN"))) AS warns
  count(eval(searchmatch("INFO"))) AS infos

samples.title: Sample - Multiple Append Pattern

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined NOT * | stats count by status

samples.explanation: NOT * combined with an index filter without parentheses evaluates with surprising precedence — wrong results, no error. Parenthesize, or use inclusion.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined (status=404 OR status=500) | stats count by status

samples.title: Sample - Unparenthesized NOT Star

bad.spl: index=web | table clientip, status, uri_path | search status=404 | stats count by clientip

samples.explanation: table mid-pipeline is a transforming command — it centralizes and strips fields before the filter runs. fields (distributable) trims columns without the barrier; better yet, filter first.

good.spl: index=web status=404 | stats count by clientip

samples.title: Sample - Premature Table Command

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by clientip, status | search status=500

samples.explanation: stats before the status filter transforms the entire candidate set on the search head, then throws most of it away. Filter in the base search first.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined status=500 | stats count by clientip

samples.title: Sample - Premature Transform

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | rex "a=(?<a>\S+)" | rex "b=(?<b>\S+)" | rex "c=(?<c>\S+)"

samples.explanation: Each rex re-reads the source field per event; several in sequence multiply parse passes that one combined pattern would do once (low: cost only).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | rex "a=(?<a>\S+) b=(?<b>\S+) c=(?<c>\S+)"

samples.title: Sample - Sequential Rex Commands

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | sort 0 _time | transaction clientip maxspan=30m

samples.explanation: A sort barrier stacked in front of the already-expensive transaction — two SH-bound buffering passes; usually a smell that stats is the right tool.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats earliest(_time) AS s latest(_time) AS e by clientip

samples.title: Sample - Sort Before Transaction

bad.spl: index=web | stats count by host, sourcetype

samples.explanation: Counting by indexed fields only (host, sourcetype) never needs _raw — tstats answers from tsidx alone, routinely 10-100x faster.

good.spl: | tstats count where index=web by host, sourcetype

samples.title: Sample - Stats Instead of Tstats

bad.spl: index=auth action=failure [search index=threat_intel | fields src_ip] | stats count by src_ip

samples.explanation: The threat-intel subsearch is re-run on every execution and silently capped at 10k results / 60s. A lookup holds the same IOC set with no cap and no per-run dispatch.

good.spl: index=auth action=failure [| inputlookup threat_intel_iocs | fields src_ip] | stats count by src_ip

samples.title: Sample - Subsearch Risk

bad.spl: index=web | transaction clientip maxspan=30m | stats avg(duration)

samples.explanation: transaction assembles sessions in search-head memory and silently drops events past maxopentxn/maxopenevents. stats computes the same session bounds distributably, with no eviction.

good.spl: index=web | stats earliest(_time) AS start latest(_time) AS end BY clientip | eval duration=end-start | stats avg(duration)

samples.title: Sample - Transaction Overuse

bad.spl: | tstats count from datamodel=Web by sourcetype

samples.explanation: tstats over an accelerated data model without an index constraint scans all summary buckets — "it uses tstats so it's fast" is false comfort. Constrain inside where.

good.spl: | tstats count from datamodel=Web where index=web by sourcetype

samples.title: Sample - Tstats Datamodel Unscoped

samples.explanation: Indexed-fields-only reporting done right: tstats with index scope inside the where clause.

good.spl: | tstats count where index=web by host, _time span=1h

samples.title: Sample - Tstats Host Volume

bad.spl: index=* error | stats count by host

samples.explanation: index=* scans every index in the environment. Naming the index turns a platform-wide crawl into a single-index read.

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined "error" | stats count by host

samples.title: Sample - Unbounded Index Scan

bad.spl: index=web | join clientip [search index=firewall] | stats count by action

samples.explanation: join buffers its subsearch on the search head, capped at 50k rows / 60s — then truncates silently. A single pass with stats by the common key reads both datasets once and never truncates.

good.spl: (index=web) OR (index=firewall) | stats values(action) AS action dc(index) AS sources BY clientip | where sources=2 | stats count by action

samples.title: Sample - Unbounded Join

bad.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by clientip | sort -count | head 20

samples.explanation: A sort with no explicit count keeps only 10,000 rows and drops the rest before head sees them — the top-N can be computed on the wrong slice (low).

good.spl: index=web sourcetype=access_combined | stats count by clientip | sort 20 -count

samples.title: Sample - Unbounded Sort

samples.explanation: What good looks like: index + sourcetype + indexed-field filter, early field trim, aggregation last.

good.spl: index=app sourcetype=app_logs log_level=ERROR | fields _time, host, component, message | stats count BY host, component

samples.title: Sample - Well Scoped Error Report
